findings.title: Document the Windows installer recovery state where the original may exist only in the destination-local backup
findings.evidence: After File.Replace reports a failure or the installed-hash check throws, recovery removes the target before moving the destination-local backup back. If that Move also fails, the target can be absent while the original bytes remain only at .llmgw-backup-*. The script preserves and prints backup/candidate paths through replace_failed_recovery_unconfirmed, but the Windows installation instructions do not explain this partial-failure state or the required recovery action.
findings.reproduction: Source branch: product/packaging/install.ps1:111-117 removes target then moves backup; lines 131-135 preserveRecovery=true and report paths when recovery is unconfirmed. PowerShell/Windows execution was unavailable, so this is static control-flow evidence rather than a Windows runtime reproduction.
findings.required_change: Add a Windows-specific recovery paragraph: on replace_failed_recovery_unconfirmed, stop and preserve the reported files; the previous executable may be only at the reported destination-local .llmgw-backup-* path while llmgw.exe is absent, and the candidate may also remain. Explain how to identify/restore the previous file without deleting either recovery copy, and keep Windows runtime status explicitly unverified.
